previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and known marginal ulcer history was admitted for 5 days of epigastric/right and left upper quadrant abdominal pain with nausea, diarrhea, and dark guaiac-positive stools. She received IV fluids and symptom control, and Gastroenterology performed EGD showing gastritis, a new small ulcer at the gastrojejunal anastomosis, improvement of a larger known anastomotic ulcer, and resolution of a previously seen smaller ulcer; pantoprazole was increased to 40 mg twice daily and sucralfate was continued. Stool testing was negative for H. pylori antigen and two C. difficile toxin tests were negative. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast showed no bowel obstruction and noted a small left renal hypoattenuation focus without supportive urinalysis findings. Hematocrit was monitored for possible GI bleeding and stabilized/normalized prior to discharge; pain control was transitioned from IV morphine to oral hydromorphone with good effect. She was discharged home tolerating a regular diet, ambulating independently, with plans for repeat EGD in 6 weeks and surgical follow-up within 2 weeks, and return precautions for bleeding or worsening symptoms.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ lady with status post Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
complicated by marginal ulcers with inability to consume adequate oral intake,
for tunneled access line for TPN.

MEDICATIONS:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
200 mcg of fentanyl and 4 mg of midazolam throughout the total intraservice
time of 25 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored.  1% lidocaine was used for local pain control.  1%
lidocaine with epinephrine was used in the creation of the subcutaneous tunnel
in the right upper chest.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ (fellow).  Dr. ___ (attending
interventional radiologist) reviewed the images:

PROCEDURES:
1.  Right internal jugular venous access.
2.  Placement of a 10 ___ double-lumen catheter with a 20-cm tip-to-cuff
measurement.
3.  Post-procedure spot fluoroscopic image.

TECHNIQUE AND FINDINGS:  After description of the procedure and discussion of
the risks, benefits, and alternatives to the procedure with the patient,
written informed consent was obtained.  The patient was brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The right upper
neck was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A preprocedure
timeout and huddle were performed per ___ protocol.

Under sonographic guidance, with hard copy images on file, the right internal
jugular vein was punctured with a 21-gauge needle, after local pain control
was induced with 1% lidocaine.  A 0.018 wire was advanced into the SVC under
fluoroscopic guidance.  A skin ___ was made.  The needle was removed and a
4.5 ___ micropuncture sheath advanced over the wire.  The wire and inner
dilator were removed and a 0.035 ___ wire advanced into the SVC and
appropriate measurements taken.  The wire was replaced and advanced into the
IVC.  Next, attention was turned to the creation of a subcutaneous tunnel. 
Approximately four fingerbreadths below the venopuncture site, a 1-cm incision
was made after instillation of 1% lidocaine and 1% lidocaine with epinephrine
along the proposed subcutaneous tunnel tract.  Next, the appropriately sized
10 ___ double-lumen catheter was advanced along the created subcutaneous
tunnel and port at the venopuncture site.  Next, the micropuncture sheath was
removed and a peel-away sheath advanced over the wire.  The wire and inner
dilator were removed.  The catheter was advanced through the peel-away sheath
and the peel-away sheath removed.  

A fluoroscopic post-procedure spot image demonstrated the tip of the catheter
to be in the superior right atrium.  The catheter was attached to the skin
with 0 silk suture.  The venotomy site was closed with a 4-Vicryl suture. 
Both ports aspirated and flushed easily.  Sterile dressings were applied.  The
patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated insertion of a tunneled 10 ___ double-lumen
catheter, 20 cm tip-to-cuff, with tip located in the right atrium.  The
catheter is ready for use.

INDICATION:  ___ female with new onset dull right upper quadrant pain
in the setting of prior laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery and excessive
weight loss.  Evaluate for cholelithiasis.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen ___.

RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:

The liver is normal in size and echotexture.  There are no focal hepatic
lesions identified.  There is no biliary ductal dilation.  The common bile
duct measures 5 mm.  The gallbladder contains no stones or sludge, and there
is no gallbladder wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid to suggest acute
cholecystitis.  There is normal antegrade portal flow.  

The midline structures, including the pancreas and aorta, are obscured by
bowel gas.   The intrahepatic IVC is normal in caliber.  The spleen is not
enlarged, measuring 10.1 cm.  There is no ascites. 

IMPRESSION:  No cholelithiasis or other sonographic explanation for patient's
upper abdominal pain.
